summary: The root نَمَم primarily refers to carrying tales or slander, especially with the intent to cause mischief or discord between people.

provenance.lane: Edward William Lane, An Arabic-English Lexicon (1863-93), public domain. Digital text via Perseus, Tufts University, CC BY-SA 3.0 US.
provenance.summary: Editorial summary derived from the Lane entry. NOT Lane's own wording. Shown as a gloss only; the Lane text below is the source.

headwords.gloss: uttered calumny; excited discord; dissension, and made known discourse in a mischievous manner

told, conversation, in a malicious or mischievous manner, so as to occasion discord, dissension, or the like.

headwords.def: نَمَّ He [ uttered calumny: or] excited discord, or dissension, and made known discourse in a mischievous manner; or embellished speech with falsehood. (M, K.) You say, نَمَّ بِهِ and عَلَيْهِ , inf. n. نَمٌّ and نَمِيمَةٌ and نَمِيمٌ , or this last is pl. of نَمِيمَةٌ , (M,) meaning, He calumniated him; or misrepresented him. نَمَّ الحَدِيثَ He made known, divulged, or told, conversation, in a malicious or mischievous manner, so as to occasion discord, dissension, or the like. (TA, art. قت ; and Msb. *)
R. Q. 1 نَمْنَمَ He variegated a thing: he decorated or embellished it. (S, K.)

parts.t: of the skull; as resembling lines of writing; see

headwords.def: نَمَانِمُ The sutures of the skull; as resembling lines of writing; see شَأْنٌ .
نَمَّامٌ now commonly applied to Wild thyme, thymus serpyllum: see شَبَهَانٌ .
نَامَّةٌ The artery in the head: see أَبْهَرُ .

headwords.def: مُنَمْنَمٌ A garment, or piece of cloth, figured with marks resembling writing, or otherwise. See مَذَبَّرٌ .
